items.prose: A volatility forecaster is trained in two set-ups, P and Q, on six seeds; seed $i$ gives both the same weights and batches. The table holds each run's validation loss.

parts.question: What is the mean of the differences Q minus P? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.correct: The differences sum to -0.073, so $\bar d = -0.0122$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Subtract P from Q seed by seed, then average.

byKey.sign: Q minus P is negative here.

parts.question: Using $\bar d = -0.0122$ from part 1, what is $s_d$, dividing by $n - 1$? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Squared deviations of the differences, over 5.

explain.text: The squared deviations of the six differences from -0.0122 sum to 0.000233; over 5 and rooted that is 0.0068.

parts.question: With $s_d = 0.0068$ from part 2, what is the paired $t$? Give 2 decimal places.

explain.text: The standard error is $0.0068/\sqrt 6 = 0.00279$, and $-0.0122$ over it is -4.37.

parts.question: Take $t_{0.975,\,5} = 2.571$. What is the upper end of the 95% interval for the mean difference? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the half-width to $\bar d$.

byKey.sign: The upper end is still below 0.

explain.text: The half-width is 0.0072, so the interval runs from -0.0193 to -0.0050.

options.text: On these six seeds Q lowers the loss; the whole 95% interval is below 0
No difference: the means of P and Q are within one sd of each other
options.why: That compares the groups as if unpaired; within pairs Q wins on every seed.

options.text: P is better, since its losses are larger
options.why: A lower loss is better: Q wins.

feedback.correct: The paired interval excludes 0: Q is better on these seeds.

explain.text: The interval lies below 0, so the gain is real on these seeds. A new split or data set could still change it.

items.prose: A credit model's full set-up and the same set-up with change X removed are trained on five shared seeds. Full: 0.25, 0.27, 0.24, 0.26, 0.28. Without X: 0.29, 0.30, 0.28, 0.31, 0.32.

parts.question: What is X's effect, the mean of (without X) minus (full)? Give 3 decimal places.

feedback.correct: The differences are 0.04, 0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.04; their mean is 0.040.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Pair by seed, subtract, average.

byKey.sign: Without minus full is positive: X helped.

explain.text: Seed by seed the loss rises by 0.04, 0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.04 without X, a mean of 0.040.

parts.question: Using the differences behind the 0.040 of part 1, what is their sd, dividing by $n - 1$? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.correct: $s = 0.0071$: every seed agrees within a hundredth.

explain.text: The squared deviations from 0.04 sum to 0.0002; over 4 that is 0.00005, and the root is 0.0071.

parts.question: Another table gives mean losses: base 0.36, with X only 0.33, with Y only 0.34, with both 0.27. What is the interaction, X's effect with Y on minus its effect with Y off? Give 2 decimal places, with its sign.

feedback.generic: Not quite. X's effect in each column.

byKey.sign: With Y on minus with Y off.
byKey.both: That is both against the base.

explain.text: X lowers the loss by 0.03 alone and by 0.07 with Y, so they help more together: $-0.04$.

parts.question: An ablation in both directions of 4 changes, every row on 5 seeds, runs the full set-up, 4 removals, the baseline and 4 additions. How many training runs is that?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the rows, times 5.

explain.text: Ten rows of 5 seeds: 50 runs, against 80 for every one of the $2^4 = 16$ mixes.

items.prose: A rates model is retrained on five seeds with the split held fixed. Its validation losses are 0.142, 0.131, 0.155, 0.138 and 0.149.

parts.question: What is the mean? Give 3 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add and divide by 5.

byKey.best: That is the best seed, not the mean.

explain.text: The five sum to 0.715, so the mean is 0.143.

parts.question: Using the mean of 0.143 from part 1, what is the sd, dividing by $n - 1$? Give 4 decimal places.

explain.text: The squared deviations sum to 0.000350; over 4 and rooted, 0.0094.

parts.question: With the sd 0.0094 from part 2, how many sds below the mean is the best seed? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. The gap over the sd.

byKey.gap: Divide the gap by the sd.

explain.text: The best seed sits 0.012 below the mean, which is 1.28 sds: a lucky draw, not the model's level.

parts.question: The team's log shows they reported seed 2's 0.131 and scored the test set after each of the five runs. Which fault matters most for the reported test score?

options.text: The test set was scored five times, so it helped choose the reported run
Seed 2's value was not written in the training log
options.why: The seed is in the log; the issue is how it was chosen.

options.text: The mean of the five was rounded to 3 places

feedback.correct: Five test scores means the test set took part in the choice.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the test scores.

explain.text: Picking the best of five and scoring the test set each time makes the test score optimistic. Report the five-seed mean and score the test set once.
